objective: By the end of the lesson, learners will have practised and developed the sub-skills of reading for gist and detailed comprehension in the context of an introduction to A Monster Calls by Patrick Ness.
materials:
- A Monster Calls by Patrick Ness (Chapters 1 & 2)
- YouTube trailer: A Monster Calls - Official Trailer (2016) — https://youtu.be/R2Xbo-irtBA
- Chapters 1-2 booklet (includes reflection questions)
- Composite film image / author photo

stages.stage_aim: To activate learners' interest in the novel and build anticipation.
stages.procedure:
- Show the A Monster Calls trailer (~2 min).
- Elicit initial reactions: 'What do you think this story is about?'
- Pair discussion: 'What would you do if a monster came to your window at midnight?'
- Brief class feedback (2 min).
- Bridge to the novel: 'A Monster Calls is about a boy named Conor who is visited by a monster — a yew tree that walks and talks. But this monster wants something more frightening than Conor expects. Today we read Chapters 1 & 2 together.'

stages.stage: Author Spotlight — Patrick Ness & Siobhan Dowd
stages.stage_aim: To give learners context about the authors and the novel's unique origin.
stages.procedure:
- Present Patrick Ness facts: born 1971 in the US, moved to the UK.
- Awards: A Monster Calls won the Carnegie Medal (2012) and the Kate Greenaway Medal — the only book ever to win both. Ness won the Carnegie two years in a row, only the second author to do so.
- Sales: Over 1 million copies sold worldwide, translated into 30+ languages.
- Show composite film image and author photo.
- Pre-teach selected vocabulary: yew, shimmering, ancient, untamed, compost (brief board presentation with context from the chapter).

stages.stage: Setting the Purpose — Why Read Aloud?
stages.stage_aim: To establish the rationale for the reading circle format.
stages.procedure:
- Elicit: 'Why do we read out loud together in a reading circle?'
- Highlight benefits: improves fluency, builds vocabulary through context, creates a shared experience, helps hear the natural rhythm of English.
- Explain the lesson format: 20 min guided read-aloud, followed by private reading with reflection questions.

stages.stage_aim: To guide learners through the opening chapters of the novel and develop reading fluency.
stages.procedure:
- Teacher and students take turns reading paragraphs aloud — each student reads 1-2 paragraphs then passes.
- Pause after the opening lines of Chapter 1: 'The monster showed up just after midnight. As they do.' Ask: 'What is effective about this opening? How does it make you feel?'
- Pause after 'He'd told no one about the nightmare': 'Why do you think Conor keeps the nightmare a secret? What might it be about?'
- Pause when Conor says 'Not of you, anyway': 'Why isn't Conor afraid of the monster? What could he be more afraid of?'
- Draw attention to the yew tree as the monster — a symbol from nature connected to the mother's illness.
- Discuss the final line of Chapter 1: 'You will be. Before the end.' What does the monster mean?
- Continue into Chapter 2 (BREAKFAST). Pause after Conor cleans up the yew leaves: 'Why is Conor hiding the evidence? Why doesn't he tell anyone?'
- Pause after Conor's mother says 'I wish you didn't have to be quite so good': 'What does this tell us about Conor's life? How is he different from a normal thirteen-year-old?'

stages.stage_aim: To give learners time to absorb the text individually and respond personally.
stages.procedure:
- Students re-read the chapter silently or continue from where the read-aloud stopped.
- Hand out reflection questions.
- Students write answers for themselves — this is not assessed, just a way to think about the text.
- If time permits, invite 1-2 students to share one thing they wrote with the class.

reflection_questions: 1. Conor hides the yew leaves in the bin and lies to his mother about hearing him last night. Why do you think he keeps the monster a secret? What would you do if a monster visited you?
2. Conor's mother says 'I wish you didn't have to be quite so good.' What does this tell us about Conor's life at home? How has his life changed since his mother became ill?
